newsitem.title: FRANCE: France thinks Nigeria to restore order in Freetown.
newsitem.headline: France thinks Nigeria to restore order in Freetown.

text.p: France believes Nigerian troops will restore order within days in Sierra Leone, where an army coup has overthrown the civilian government, a senior French defence ministry official said on Thursday.
"You surely must be aware that Nigerian troops are arriving in force in Freetown and one can estimate order will be restored there in the coming days," the officer told a press briefing.
Nigeria has made no public statement on Sunday's coup but officials said it was trying to negotiate a peaceful restoration of civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
The French officer was answering questions about the safety of some 100 French nationals in Sierre Leone who have been urged to leave the country by their government.
He said an agreement was reached with the United States that the French would be evacuated by American troops if the need arose.
The U.S. Navy helicopter ship Kearsarge, presumably with Marine units aboard, was off Sierra Leone's coast ready to evacuate U.S. and other foreigners from the troubled West African state.
